newsitem.title: USA: Sabre says AMR could spin off rest.
newsitem.headline: Sabre says AMR could spin off rest.

text.p: Sabre Group Holdings Inc, which is majority-owned by AMR Corp, said AMR could sell off the rest of its holdings in the reservation and information systems company.
AMR gained $592 million in net proceeds when it sold about 18 percent of Sabre Group in an initial public offering last October.
"In these types of carve out IPOs . . . it would be relatively uncommon for the parent company not to sell or distribute the rest," Michael Durham, Sabre's chief executive told Reuters.
"If history is any indicator, the current state would probably not be the steady state," Durham said.
AMR's decision to sell the remaining stake in Sabre would likely be contingent on the deal being structured as tax-free, Durham said.

At the time of Sabre's IPO, some industry analysts said they expected AMR to eventually sell the balance of its Sabre holdings. AMR, the parent of American Airlines, could not be immediately reached for comment.
Sabre is the largest distributor of travel data in the U.S. and also provides information technology solutions for the travel industry.
